paragraphs:
R' Yehudah ben Levi.
(Hyman classifies him as a Jerusalem Talmud amora of the first generation.)
As in [Jerusalem Talmud Demai 5:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Demai.5.8.8): Rabbi Zeira said, Abba Antoli bought produce from Arameans; he came to Rabbi Yudah ben Levi, who sent word to his son Menahem to set it right for him. He gave him its tithes (Hyman adds: for he was a Levite). When he arrived, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi stood with him and said to him: Who would do this but your father? (Hyman suggests: perhaps they were brothers.)
And R' Yohanan inquired of him, as in [Shabbat 113a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.113a.10) and [Niddah 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.60a.16): R' Yochanan inquired of R' Yehudah bar Liva'i.

And it is cited in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat ch. 7, end of halakhah 1, in the wording: R' Yochanan asked R' Yehudah ben Levi (Hyman argues: from this we see that he is one person, and [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1686&lang=en) needlessly divided them into two).

Likewise he is mentioned in [Arakhin 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.16b.3), where he expounded why the Torah distinguishes the leper, that it says he shall bring two birds, etc. (and some read there R' Yehoshua ben Levi).

And in Shabbat ch. 7, end of halakhah 2, and [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.1.8): R' Hizkiah, R' Yehudah ben Levi, R' Yehoshua ben Levi in the name of Rabbi.

As for what we find in [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.8.3), R"Y b"L in the name of R' Alexandri, and the statement is cited in [Pesikta Rabbati, “In the Seventh Month”](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesikta_Rabbati.40), section 3, in the name of R' Yehudah ben Levi — Hyman concludes that without doubt it should be reversed, for R' Alexandri was much later than he. Those who say [teachings] in his name we find in [Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 2:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.2.8.3): R' Hizkiah, R' Aha in his name; but in Terumot ch. 5, halakhah 4 the reading is R' Yudah son of R' Hanina.
And in Shabbat ch. 7, halakhah 2 [final locator ‘־ל.’ unclear; [compare Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.7.2.54)]: R' Yose, R' Aha in his name.[^5]

notes.text: RI in the paragraph explicitly introducing Rabbi Yochanan is Rabbi Yochanan. Pesikta ס״ג is section3, not63; ע״ש marks attribution, not see there.

The Demai tithe-recipient roles, final locator ה״ב־ל and Alexandri transmission chain remain source questions. The brother hypothesis, name forms, chronology and proposed reversal are Hyman’s arguments.

The named Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Demai 5:8 paragraph explicitly gives Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Yudah ben Levi, Menahem his son, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, with the question ‘Who would do this but your father?’ The paragraph also disputes that wording and supplies an alternative; that alternative is not substituted for Hyman’s quotation. The Hebrew pronouns and tithe-recipient roles remain source questions, and Hyman’s parenthetical Levite explanation and tentative brother suggestion remain his claims. The digital form Yudah and Hyman’s Yehudah/Yudah and ben/bar Livai forms are retained without harmonization. The first-generation classification, one-person argument against Sefer ha-Dorot, and emphatic ‘without doubt’ chronological reversal of the Alexandri chain are attributed to Hyman at their supplied force. The end-of-halakhah qualifiers are restored from סה״א and סה״ב, without claiming modern numbering verification. The final ה״ב־ל. locator remains unresolved. The source’s רבי is rendered Rabbi, without the earlier supplied identification as Yehudah the Prince; other titles not locally collated remain R'. Both preceding mixed notes are preserved. No identity, kinship or chronological binding follows from these comparisons.

In his English Demai 5:8 translation and note 123, Guggenheimer takes Abba to have given the tithes to Menahem. His note 122 treats the designation “ben Levi” as indicating a Levite and does not infer a family relationship between the two rabbis. The Hebrew pronouns and Hyman’s tentative suggestion are preserved. The passage itself also offers a different account of what Yehoshua said. The named Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah 4:8 reads Yehoshua ben Levi in Alexandri’s name, while the consulted passage in Pesikta Rabbati 40 has Pinchas reporting Yehudah ben Levi in Alexandri’s name. Hyman’s “without doubt” reversal remains his own proposal. The compressed final Shabbat locator remains unresolved in the printed notice (II, pp. 563–564).

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1686&lang=en) places the notice under Yehudah ben Levi, cites the two birds, and gives Demai 5:9 for the Abba Antoli episode. The linked edition places that episode at 5:8. The linked Megillah has Acha, Yudah ben Levi and Yehoshua ben Levi in the chain, where Hyman gives Hizkiah first.
